scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 at 20.1.1.x, the machine PC12 at 120.1.1.x is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped. Something around the border post must be
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the box in the middle and
get us through -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — PC0 (20.1.1.10) unable to reach PC12 (120.1.1.10) — is not confirmed by any live evidence. A full topology-wide reachability sweep showed 0% packet loss in both directions with sub-4 ms RTT, ruling out any current data-plane failure.

A thorough four-phase broad search was performed. Phase A (L2/infrastructure): `infra_sweep` and `l2_snapshot` found zero addressing anomalies, zero ACL drop rules, and no duplicate MACs across all 15 devices. Phase B (routing/control-plane): `ospf_snapshot` flagged r8, r12, and r13; each flag was individually confirmed as a normal design characteristic. R8 is a valid OSPF ABR with a virtual link to r4 through area 0.0.0.1 and a stub leaf area 0.0.0.2 on its BB segment — `show ip ospf neighbor detail` confirmed Full adjacencies to both r5 (area 0.0.0.1) and r4 (backbone via VLINK0); area 0.0.0.2 networks (80.0.0.0/8) propagate correctly throughout the OSPF domain. R12 runs EIGRP (not OSPF) and uses a kernel static default route toward r11; r13 is similarly EIGRP-only. The OSPF–EIGRP redistribution boundary at r11 is functioning: r11 redistributes 120.0.0.0/8 (pc12's subnet, learned via EIGRP from r12) into OSPF, and r1's routing table confirms a live `O>* 120.0.0.0/8 via r11`. `tc_snapshot` found only default fq_codel qdiscs. Phase D (service/resource): `pressure_sweep` was clean on all devices; no web services exist in this topology.

Root cause: No fault is present. The network is operating as designed. The user's report may reflect a transient disruption that has since self-resolved, or confusion with a different destination or service.

Fix: No corrective action required.
